chunks: What was narrated by Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Jamil ibn Darrāj, from Zurārah, who said:
I heard Abā Ja'far عليه السلام say: “The 'iddah and menstruation are referred to the women.”

Because the manner of reconciling between them is that if the woman is trusted, her statement regarding the 'iddah and menstruation is accepted; and if she is under suspicion, other women are tasked [to verify], according to what the first report contained.

key_terms.النِّسَاءِ: women, indicating their authority in reporting these matters
key_terms.الْحَيْضُ: menstruation, with legal implications for ritual and family law
key_terms.الْخَبَرُ الْأَوَّلُ: the earlier report to which this explanation refers
key_terms.الْعِدَّةُ: the waiting period observed by a woman after divorce or widowhood
key_terms.قُبِلَ قَوْلُهَا: her statement is accepted as legally valid
key_terms.مَأْمُونَةً: trusted and considered reliable in her statement
key_terms.مُتَّهَمَةً: under suspicion or not accepted without further verification

ai.seo_question: When is a woman's statement accepted regarding 'iddah and menstruation in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith states a legal principle that matters of 'iddah and menstruation are primarily established through the woman's own statement. It also indicates that when she is trusted her word is accepted, but if suspicion exists, verification through other women may be required.
